name: Zhou Enlai
summary: Chinese Communist leader and first premier of the People's Republic, a Marxist-Leninist who defended party-led socialism, the dictatorship of the proletariat and state ownership while pursuing pragmatic diplomacy on the basis of the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence. He backed regional autonomy for minorities within a unitary state and economic modernization.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: In November 1937 he argues for persisting in the war of resistance against the Japanese occupation in North China instead of seeking peace by compromise.

arms-reduction.rationale: At Bandung he reports the world's peoples' demand for reducing armaments and in 1964 he proposes complete prohibition of nuclear weapons.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: His 1975 report contrasts China's balance of revenue and expenditure and absence of debts with the turmoil and inflation of capitalist countries.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: His 1975 report says the struggle between the proletariat and bourgeoisie and between socialist and capitalist roads is long and at times acute, and calls for continuing the revolution under the dictatorship of the proletariat.

collective-farming.rationale: The same 1953 speech makes collectivizing agriculture and handicrafts part of the transition, and his 1975 report praises the people's commune as proven superior.

colonial-socialism-democratic-stage.rationale: His 1944 Sixth Congress talk and 1949 texts set New Democracy as the stage before socialism, and in 1953 he recalls the Common Programme did so.

death-penalty.rationale: He reports that death sentences went to those who had directly oppressed the people and committed murder and had not confessed.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He describes the Chinese state as in essence the dictatorship of the proletariat and, in 1975, calls for consolidating it down to the grass roots.

dominated-front.rationale: At Bandung he urges Asian and African countries scarred by colonial rule to unite for independence and cooperation, while saying they have no wish to set them against other regions.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: His 1959 government report endorses the suppression of the Tibetan rebellion and dissolution of the former Tibetan government as a defence of national unity, and he left force open for Taiwan.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: At Bandung he says Asian and African countries demand economic as well as political independence and must escape being producers of raw materials for others.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: His 1964 telegram says China was compelled to test and develop nuclear weapons for defence against the US threat.

indirect-election.rationale: In 1956 he says direct secret-ballot elections were not yet introduced nationwide because the economy and culture were undeveloped, and he defends congresses chosen through the system.

land-redistribution.rationale: He says agrarian reform confiscates landlords' land and distributes it to peasants and calls it China's most acute class struggle since the war.

limit-population.rationale: In 1965 he calls family planning of great importance, with preferential treatment for those practising it, but on a voluntary basis with no coercion.

minority-language-support.rationale: In 1957 he says minority nationalities' use of their own languages must be respected and that groups lacking a script should be helped to create one.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: He describes and defends the system of autonomous regions, prefectures and counties for minority nationalities as suited to China.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: He says minorities' own languages, customs and identity must be respected and that cadres from each nationality should lead its autonomous area.

national-resource-control.rationale: At Bandung he lists Iran's struggle for sovereignty over its petroleum and Egypt's over the Suez zone among causes that Asian and African states support.

national-self-determination.rationale: At Bandung he says all dependent peoples should enjoy national self-determination, while at home in 1957 he rules out separation for China's nationalities.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: At Bandung he criticizes foreign military bases set up on Asian and African soil and backs the Geneva terms barring foreign bases in the Indo-Chinese states.

one-party-rule.rationale: He presents the state as led by the Communist Party with the democratic parties joined in a united front under its lead, and wanted opinions that go against socialism excluded.

party-commands-army.rationale: In December 1957 he tells army officers the army is led by the Party and calls for strengthening the Party's leadership over it.

party-own-road.rationale: In his 1960 talk on the Comintern he faults it for instructing individual parties and insists each party must think independently about revolution in its own country.

public-ownership.rationale: In his 1953 speech on the general line he calls the abolition of private capital's ownership of the means of production in favour of state ownership the quintessence of socialism.

rehabilitation.rationale: In 1956 he reports that more counter-revolutionaries were reformed through labour than executed and urges leniency to win acceptance of remoulding.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: He calls peaceful unification of Korea the right solution at Bandung and, for Taiwan, an unshakable national aim, but the statement stresses a border drawn by an outside power.

right-to-secede.rationale: In 1957 he says China deliberately did not adopt the Soviet option of separation for nationalities, preferring regional autonomy in a unitary multi-national state.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: In 1949 and again in December 1964 he says China must chiefly rely on its own efforts, and his 1964 eight principles on aid stress helping recipients toward self-reliance.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: His 1951 directive as premier to enforce the Marriage Law describes the new family as based on equality and condemns forced and mercenary marriage.

state-class-instrument.rationale: In 1956 he says the capitalist parliamentary system is a dictatorship of the exploiting classes and that China's state exercises dictatorship over remaining exploiting classes.

state-directs-investment.rationale: His 1975 report sets national plans with fixed priorities (agriculture, light industry, heavy industry) and a state-drawn ten-year plan aimed at industry and defence.

suppress-opposition.rationale: In 1956 he reports the campaigns to suppress counter-revolutionaries and says opposing views are allowed only where they do not go against socialism.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: In 1972 he orders that beating and other maltreatment of prisoners be abolished again and that violators be punished according to law.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: He describes the state as led by the working class and based on the worker-peasant alliance (1950), and repeats it in 1975.

workers-anti-imperialist-capitalist-alli.rationale: His 1944 Sixth Congress talk and late-1940s texts defend the united front with the national bourgeoisie against imperialism and feudalism.

notes: Answers rest on his own speeches and directives in the Selected Works and the 1975 and 1959 government reports. Most statements (religion, speech, markets, social issues, many foreign-policy items) are null: no stated position on the specific statement was found. Themes searched: ownership, party and state, nationalities, foreign policy, nuclear weapons, family, justice, economy, culture.
